parameters.sqlQuery:
-- Org Browser roster, rebuilt from the HR source that backs the Org Browser
-- export. Mapping decoded from your own org_browser_search_report_*.csv files
-- and cross-checked against internal schema documentation.
--
-- VERIFIED sources:
--   tbl_employee             EmID EmFirstName EmLastName EmHRISID EmExtension
--                            EmEmailAddress EmSamAccountName EmStartDate
--                            EmSeniorityDate EmForecastEndDate EmBirthday
--                            EmWgID EmEtpID EmTltID EmEmlID EmMgrID
--                            EmShirtSize EmActive
--   tblpl_workgroup          WgID WgName WgParentWgID WgActive
--                            (WgParentWgID verified from the SchemaSpy definitions of
--                             spListWorkGroupHierarchy, fnGetSubWgIDList and
--                             spRainierAllowance; root rows have WgParentWgID = 0)
--   tbl_job_title            TltID TltName TltRnkID
--   tblpl_employee_rank      RnkID RnkLevel
--   tblpl_employee_location  EmlID EmlName EmlEprID
--   tblpl_employee_type      EtpID EtpName
--   tblpl_employee_profile   EprID EprName
--
-- LEAST CERTAIN PART - the three NetSuite tables feeding Headcount
-- Classification. Their COLUMN names are verified ("Org Designer - Talent") but
-- they are documented under a different project, so they may not exist in
-- sql-data-prod.csn_hr. If this query errors with "Not found: Table ...
-- netsuite ...", delete the block marked HEADCOUNT CLASSIFICATION BLOCK below
-- plus the headcount_classification select line. Everything else keeps working.
--
-- SCOPE: Frontline only - active employees at or under workgroup 12056.
--
-- Still unsourced, so they arrive blank: Home Department, Reporting VP,
-- Reporting Senior VP, Term Date, Work Group 20. Work Group 20 is blank in every
-- row of your own exports too (the deepest path observed uses 9 levels).

WITH RECURSIVE
wg AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(WgID AS INT64)                              AS wgid,
    TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(WgName AS STRING), ''))       AS wgname,
    CAST(WgParentWgID AS INT64)                      AS parent_wgid
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tblpl_workgroup`
),
-- Walk each workgroup up to its root, accumulating "Name (ID)" leaf-first.
climb AS (
  SELECT
    w.wgid AS leaf_wgid, w.wgid, w.parent_wgid, 1 AS depth,
    [CONCAT(w.wgname, ' (', CAST(w.wgid AS STRING), ')')] AS chain
  FROM wg AS w
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    c.leaf_wgid, p.wgid, p.parent_wgid, c.depth + 1,
    ARRAY_CONCAT(c.chain, [CONCAT(p.wgname, ' (', CAST(p.wgid AS STRING), ')')])
  FROM climb AS c
  JOIN wg AS p ON p.wgid = c.parent_wgid
  WHERE c.parent_wgid IS NOT NULL AND c.parent_wgid <> 0 AND c.depth < 20
),
-- Keep the longest walk per workgroup, then reverse it to root-first order.
wg_path AS (
  SELECT leaf_wgid, ARRAY_REVERSE(chain) AS path
  FROM climb
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY leaf_wgid ORDER BY depth DESC) = 1
),
-- ============================ SCOPE: FRONTLINE ============================
-- Everyone at or beneath workgroup 12056, the Frontline org root.
--
-- Why the ID and not the name: 12056 reads "Execute - NA Service" in the
-- 2026-03 and 2026-05 exports and "Frontline Service Ops" in 2026-08. Same
-- node, renamed. Matching on WgName LIKE '%Frontline%' would break on that
-- rename AND would drop NA CARE (6494), Multiple Contacts (17384) and
-- B2B and Canada (16358), which are Frontline sub-orgs whose names never say
-- "Frontline". Anchoring on the ID as an ancestor survives renames and picks
-- up new teams automatically after a reorg.
--
-- TO CHANGE SCOPE, edit this one array:
--   [12056]                 Frontline org only                    (current)
--   [12056, 16188]          + SLD Offshore Profiles (ISL/ESL frontline contractors)
--   [6410]                  all of Global Service
--   [16409]                 US Frontline subtree only
--
-- NOTE on offshore: the ISL/ESL frontline agents in your exports
-- ("Service Associate Voice NA Contingent" etc.) do NOT sit under 12056. They
-- hang off Enterprise -> Finance -> BPO Management -> Offshore Profiles (11773)
-- -> SLD Offshore Profiles (16188). They are excluded as written. If your
-- frontline includes them, use [12056, 16188].
scope_roots AS (
  SELECT wgid FROM UNNEST([12056]) AS wgid
),
in_scope_wgs AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.leaf_wgid AS wgid
  FROM climb AS c
  WHERE c.wgid IN (SELECT wgid FROM scope_roots)
)
-- ========================== END SCOPE DEFINITION ==========================

SELECT
  CAST(e.EmID AS STRING)                                  AS employee_id,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(e.EmFirstName AS STRING), ''))       AS preferred_first_name,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(e.EmLastName AS STRING), ''))        AS preferred_last_name,
  CAST(e.EmHRISID AS STRING)                              AS hris_id,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(e.EmExtension AS STRING), ''))       AS phone_extension,
  LOWER(TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(e.EmEmailAddress AS STRING), ''))) AS email_address,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(e.EmSamAccountName AS STRING), ''))  AS sam_account_name,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(loc.EmlName AS STRING), ''))         AS office_location,
  IFNULL(FORMAT_DATE('%m/%d/%Y', SAFE_CAST(e.EmStartDate AS DATE)), '')       AS start_date,
  IFNULL(FORMAT_DATE('%m/%d/%Y', SAFE_CAST(e.EmSeniorityDate AS DATE)), '')   AS seniority_date,
  IFNULL(FORMAT_DATE('%m/%d/%Y', SAFE_CAST(e.EmForecastEndDate AS DATE)), '') AS forecast_end_date,
  IFNULL(FORMAT_DATE('%b %d', SAFE_CAST(e.EmBirthday AS DATE)), '')           AS birthday,
  CAST(e.EmWgID AS STRING)                                AS work_group_id,
  ewg.wgname                                              AS work_group,
  -- Parent Work Group is the NAME only in the export, no trailing "(ID)"
  TRIM(COALESCE(pwg.wgname, ''))                          AS parent_work_group,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(etp.EtpName AS STRING), ''))         AS employee_type,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(epr.EprName AS STRING), ''))         AS employee_profile,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(jt.TltName AS STRING), ''))          AS job_title,
  CAST(rnk.RnkLevel AS STRING)                            AS level,
  -- HEADCOUNT CLASSIFICATION (COGS / Semi-Variable / Fixed Opex)
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(hcc.HeadcountClassificationName AS STRING), '')) AS headcount_classification,
  -- Home Department may be nsdp.NsdpName, but it is blank for most employees in
  -- your exports, which a department name would not be. Left unsourced rather
  -- than guessed. To test: uncomment the next line and add 'Home Department'
  -- to HEADER_TO_FIELD in the mapping node.
  -- TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(nsdp.NsdpName AS STRING), '')) AS home_department,
  CAST(e.EmMgrID AS STRING)                               AS manager_employee_id,
  -- Org Browser renders manager names as "Last, First"
  TRIM(CONCAT(
    TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(m.EmLastName AS STRING), '')), ', ',
    TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(m.EmFirstName AS STRING), ''))
  ))                                                      AS manager_name,
  CAST(m.EmHRISID AS STRING)                              AS manager_hris_id,
  TRIM(COALESCE(mwg.wgname, ''))                          AS manager_work_group,
  CAST(m.EmMgrID AS STRING)                               AS manager2_employee_id,
  TRIM(CONCAT(
    TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(m2.EmLastName AS STRING), '')), ', ',
    TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(m2.EmFirstName AS STRING), ''))
  ))                                                      AS manager2_name,
  CAST(m2.EmHRISID AS STRING)                             AS manager2_hris_id,
  TRIM(COALESCE(CAST(e.EmShirtSize AS STRING), ''))       AS shirt_size,
  -- Workgroup ancestor path, root first, matching "Global Business (17248)"
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(0)], '')                  AS work_group_1,
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(1)], '')                  AS work_group_2,
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(2)], '')                  AS work_group_3,
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(3)], '')                  AS work_group_4,
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(4)], '')                  AS work_group_5,
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(5)], '')                  AS work_group_6,
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(6)], '')                  AS work_group_7,
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(7)], '')                  AS work_group_8,
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(8)], '')                  AS work_group_9,
  COALESCE(wgp.path[SAFE_OFFSET(9)], '')                  AS work_group_10
FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tbl_employee` AS e
LEFT JOIN wg      AS ewg  ON ewg.wgid  = e.EmWgID
LEFT JOIN wg      AS pwg  ON pwg.wgid  = ewg.parent_wgid
LEFT JOIN wg_path AS wgp  ON wgp.leaf_wgid = e.EmWgID
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tbl_job_title`   AS jt   ON jt.TltID  = e.EmTltID
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tblpl_employee_rank`  AS rnk  ON rnk.RnkID = jt.TltRnkID
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tblpl_employee_location`  AS loc  ON loc.EmlID = e.EmEmlID
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tblpl_employee_profile`  AS epr  ON epr.EprID = loc.EmlEprID
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tblpl_employee_type`  AS etp  ON etp.EtpID = e.EmEtpID
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tbl_employee`   AS m    ON m.EmID    = e.EmMgrID
LEFT JOIN wg      AS mwg  ON mwg.wgid  = m.EmWgID
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tbl_employee`   AS m2   ON m2.EmID   = m.EmMgrID
-- >>> HEADCOUNT CLASSIFICATION BLOCK - delete these 3 joins if the tables are absent
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tbl_join_workgroup_netsuite_department`  AS jwnd ON jwnd.WgID = e.EmWgID
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tblpl_netsuite_department`  AS nsdp ON nsdp.NsdpID = jwnd.NsdpID
LEFT JOIN `wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tblpl_netsuite_head_count_classification`   AS hcc  ON hcc.HeadcountClassificationID = nsdp.HeadcountClassificationID
-- <<< END HEADCOUNT CLASSIFICATION BLOCK
WHERE e.EmActive IS TRUE
  AND e.EmID IS NOT NULL
  -- Frontline scope: see the SCOPE block above to widen or narrow
  AND e.EmWgID IN (SELECT wgid FROM in_scope_wgs)
-- Defensive: one row per employee even if a join fans out or the copy is snapshotted
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.EmID ORDER BY e.EmID) = 1
ORDER BY preferred_last_name, preferred_first_name

parameters.content:
## Org Browser Roster - Weekly Monday 4AM Arizona

Automates the manual `org_browser_search_report_*.csv` export into the sheet.

### Row 1 is the contract
The workflow READS row 1 of the tab and maps its query onto those column names. It never writes row 1 and never clears it. Reorder or rename columns in the sheet and the workflow follows. A header it cannot source yet is left blank rather than guessed at.

### Source
`wf-gcp-us-ae-sql-data-prod.csn_hr.tbl_employee` joined to tblpl_workgroup, tbl_job_title, tblpl_employee_rank, tblpl_employee_location, tblpl_employee_profile, tblpl_employee_type, plus two self-joins for the manager chain. Mapping decoded from your own exports and cross-checked against internal schema docs.

NOT the CS performance table - that table has no Shirt Size, Birthday, HRIS ID, Sam Account Name, Job Title or Level, so it can never fill this header row.

### 40 of 45 columns are populated
A WITH RECURSIVE walk over tblpl_workgroup.WgParentWgID builds the workgroup ancestor path and fills Parent Work Group plus Work Group 1-10, formatted `Name (ID)` root-first to match the export exactly.

Still blank: Home Department, Reporting VP, Reporting Senior VP, Term Date, Work Group 20. Reporting VP, Reporting Senior VP and Term Date are blank in every row of your own exports as well, so blank is faithful, not a gap. Work Group 20 is likewise always empty - the deepest path in your data uses 9 levels.

Home Department may be tblpl_netsuite_department.NsdpName; the SQL has that line commented out with instructions, since it is populated for only some of your rows and a department name would not be.

MOST LIKELY FAILURE POINT: the three NetSuite tables behind Headcount Classification. Their column names are verified but they are documented under project wf-gcp-us-aer-ta-prod, not sql-data-prod. If the run errors with "Not found: Table ... netsuite ...", delete the clearly marked HEADCOUNT CLASSIFICATION BLOCK in the SQL and its one select line. Nothing else depends on it.

### Scope: Frontline
Active employees at or beneath workgroup 12056 - the Frontline org root. All levels: agents, supervisors and managers.

Scoped by ID, not name, for two reasons. 12056 appears as "Execute - NA Service" in your 2026-03 and 2026-05 exports and "Frontline Service Ops" in 2026-08 - same node, renamed - so a name match would have broken. And NA CARE (6494), Multiple Contacts (17384) and B2B and Canada (16358) are Frontline sub-orgs whose names never contain "Frontline", so a name match would have dropped them. Anchoring on the ID also picks up new teams automatically after a reorg.

Change scope by editing one array in the SQL (SCOPE block):
  [12056]        Frontline only (current)
  [12056, 16188] + ISL/ESL offshore frontline contractors
  [6410]         all of Global Service
  [16409]        US Frontline subtree only

OFFSHORE IS EXCLUDED as written. The ISL/ESL frontline agents in your exports sit under Enterprise > Finance > BPO Management > Offshore Profiles (11773) > SLD Offshore Profiles (16188), not under 12056. Use [12056, 16188] if your frontline includes them.

For frontline AGENTS only, excluding supervisors and managers, also add:  AND rnk.RnkLevel <= 1

### Schedule
Workflow timezone `America/Phoenix`, cron `0 4 * * 1`. Arizona skips DST so this is 11:00 UTC year-round. Confirm the timezone in Workflow Settings after import.

### Safety
Zero rows from BigQuery means the sheet is NOT cleared and the run fails loudly. An empty row 1 also fails loudly instead of inventing headers. Only A2 downward is ever cleared or written.

### After import
Select credentials on the BigQuery node and both Sheets HTTP nodes. The BigQuery credential needs read access to the csn_hr dataset - the previous credential was scoped to cs_prod, so this may need a grant.
